ratification.requested: The intent key's address gains transcriptPosition (count + last id of persisted rows seen), a field the brief's literal list ({threadId, altitude, draft, attachments}) does not name.
ratification.brief_text_confirmed: brief-642.md:256-257 (§3 web item 2) gives the literal address as 'a stable hash over threadId ‖ altitude ‖ draftText ‖ sorted(attachment.document_id)' and a binding clause at :275 that only fires for a 'session-scoped or handed-out key' alternative ('you must ship a user-facing your attachment change was not resent path and a named residual').
ratification.reasoning: This closes a genuine, measured blocker the brief's literal spec did not anticipate: content-only addressing meant every repeated identical utterance ('yes' answering two different Clarify questions) collided with the first one for the life of the session, permanently, over an append-only table with no time/state bound in the door's replay lookup (0006_runtime_core.sql:954-960, `limit 1`). All four properties the brief gives reasons for in items (a)-(d) are verified still true after the change: (a) retry-reuses-key — a refused/lost send adds nothing to the transcript, so position is unchanged, confirmed by the still-green 'intent_key_survives_a_refusal' cell; (b) changed-attachment-gets-new-key — untouched, confirmed by 'THE BLOCKER'S CELL' cell; (c) distinct-resubmit pre-read — unaffected, and separately improved by ADV-642-4 in the same commit; (d) replayed:true says so once — unaffected, and separately fixed by ADV-642-2/3. Critically, this is NOT the 'session-scoped or handed-out key' alternative the brief's binding clause warns about: transcriptPosition is derived deterministically from persisted rows already in the store (never a random or server-handed value), so it does not introduce the silent-resend/silent-drop failure mode that clause exists to prevent, and the reload-recovery property (appendix C §3) is preserved for the case that actually matters (an un-admitted send). I found no DECISIONS.md ruling that conflicts with this. This is a policy/scope decision the wave owner should sign off on explicitly (as the fix round itself requests), but on the merits the reasoning holds and the fix is real, tested, and non-vacuous (independently confirmed by revert-and-red above).
